captions.detailed: A dirt-jump bike fork assembly consisting of a wide, blocky grey alloy crown and two parallel round-section legs with small dropouts at the bottom. The fork's steerer tube passes through a thick black head-tube sleeve. At the top, a grey mid-rise stem clamps a set of wide, slightly swept-back handlebars equipped with black cylindrical hand grips. The steering assembly is fully articulated, allowing the handlebars, stem, and fork to rotate as a single unit relative to the stationary head tube.
captions.instruction: Generate a 3D model of a dirt-jump bike fork and handlebar steering assembly. The model should include a blocky fork crown with two straight cylindrical legs, a central head tube, and a mid-rise stem clamping a wide handlebar with black grips, with a revolute joint enabling the steering assembly to rotate relative to the head tube.
captions.factory: The code constructs the assembly by defining three main parts: a stationary head tube, a rotating fork assembly, and a stem-and-handlebar unit. The head tube is built using a cylinder visual component. The fork is constructed by combining a box for the crown, two cylinders for the legs, box dropouts, and a cylindrical steerer tube. The handlebar assembly is built from a central stem block, a swept-back bar made of swept circles or cylinders, and cylindrical grips. A revolute joint connects the fork/steering assembly to the head tube to allow rotation, while a fixed joint positions the handlebar assembly on the steerer tube.
